title: Weekly Markets Monitor - Surprise, surprise
gist: WGC's weekly monitor says strong US data (payrolls 165k vs 70k expected) and above-target PCE mean the Fed may regret inaction and markets underpriced hikes, creating near-term headwinds for gold. Midterm results cut fiscal expansion hopes and raise AI regulation risk; oil fell sharply and the dollar strengthened.

themes.theme: Fed policy and hawkish data surprise

insights.claim: US growth data surprised strongly to the upside after the October Fed meeting, with payrolls at 165k versus 70k expected, plus lower claims, stronger hourly earnings and firmer consumer spending.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Strong labour data undercuts the case for easing and supports a hawkish repricing.

insights.claim: Inflation data since the October meeting largely met expectations, but PCE, which WGC regards as the relevant gauge, still runs well above the 2% target.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Persistent above-target PCE keeps the Fed under pressure not to ease.
insights.quote: PCE (the one that matters) continues to run well above the 2% target

insights.claim: The WGC argues the Fed may regret its inaction and that markets were wrong to downgrade the prospect of further rate hikes, implying hike risk is underpriced.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Fed funds futures may need to reprice toward tighter policy, a risk for non-yielding assets.
insights.quote: The Fed might regret its inaction, and markets their downgrading of further hikes.

insights.claim: With the policy outcome of the midterms still unclear, the strong data and hawkish repricing could create near-term macro headwinds for gold.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Near-term gold downside risk from rates, not a change in the structural case.
insights.quote: these developments could provide some near-term macro headwinds for gold

insights.claim: A softer expected US CPI print was flagged as a possible breather for gold.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A benign CPI could give short-term relief to gold.
insights.quote: Softer expected US CPI tomorrow might allow for a breather.

themes.theme: US politics, fiscal and AI regulation

insights.claim: The Democratic midterms victory tempered expectations of further US fiscal expansion while raising the prospect of tighter AI regulation.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Less fiscal stimulus and tougher AI rules weigh on growth expectations and tech valuations.
insights.quote: The Democratic midterms victory tempered expectations of further fiscal expansion while raising the prospect of tighter AI regulation.

insights.claim: Technology stocks were weak last week, and the WGC notes weaker equities may weigh on sentiment.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Equity weakness could feed risk-off flows, though the rate effect currently dominates for gold.
insights.quote: Weaker equities may weigh on sentiment

insights.claim: Last week crude oil fell sharply, bond yields declined and the US dollar strengthened, while global equities ended mixed.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A stronger dollar is another headwind for gold even as yields fell.

insights.claim: In Europe inflation edged higher and activity softened while the BoE raised rates; in Asia China's activity moderated, Japan's wage growth strengthened and India's activity stayed solid.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Divergent global growth with central banks hiking in the UK supports a broader tightening-bias narrative.
